verdict:
KILL AS A DISLOCATION, WATCH AS AN OPTION - and escalate, because both benches got a decisive number wrong in opposite directions and I had to referee with my own fetches.

THE SCREEN PREMISE IS VOID BEFORE ANY OF THIS MATTERS. The triage led with the right finding and then buried it: CLSK peaked $23.61 on 2025-10-15, the same week bitcoin topped ~$126k, and BTC is ~$64-65k now. The drawdown is roughly 1.0-beta to its own commodity. The 'excess vs Finance sector median -43.2pp' that put this name in the queue is a sector-label artifact - CLSK is tagged 'Finance: Consumer Services'. Benchmark it against BTC or the miner cohort and there is no excess drawdown to explain. There is also no forced seller anywhere in the record; the only large flow was the company buying its own stock. A dislocation needs someone selling for a reason unrelated to value, and nobody here is.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF, BECAUSE THE BENCHES CONTRADICTED EACH OTHER.

(1) BLUE IS RIGHT ON THE TEXAS OPTION, AND IT WAS SITTING IN RED'S OWN CITATION. I fetched the Sandersville lease release. It states verbatim that the tenant executed a 'letter of intent and exclusivity arrangement covering CleanSpark's entire Texas portfolio of 718 acres with up to 885 MW of secured and planned power capacity' - Sealy 271 acres / ~300MW, Brazoria 447 acres / 300MW expandable to 600MW. Red built a prize table on 175MW, declared the roof unreachable, and demoted the 885MW to a 'what would change my mind' bullet. That is a scope truncation on the decisive number, drawn from the very document red cited. Red's FATAL does not survive as stated.

(2) BLUE IS RIGHT ON THE TREASURY, AND RED'S FINDING INVERTS. Red called the marketed 13,931 BTC versus the 10-Q's 12,205 a venue-divergence where 'the vetted document choosing the smaller number is information.' I fetched the July operational update. Its own footnote reads: 'CleanSpark's Bitcoin holdings were 13,931 in total, of which 4,070 was posted as collateral or as receivable and all related to derivative transactions.' The company disclosed the encumbrance on the face of the marketed number. This is not masking - it is the ABSENCE of expected masking, which is a positive honesty datum on CLSK and should be cataloged as one. The substance is nonetheless worse than red modeled: ~29% of the treasury is encumbered, not the ~1,700 coins red inferred. Red's kg_candidate would false-positive on this exact fact pattern and must be amended before it is accepted.

(3) BLUE IS WRONG ON THE CONVERTS, AND RED WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG. Blue 'corrected' red's $14.80 conversion price to $24.05 (41.5584 shares per $1,000) and downgraded red's June-2028 put date to PLAUSIBLE for want of a clean read. I proxy-fetched the same 10-Q. The 2030 notes carry a conversion rate of 67.5858 shares per $1,000 - a conversion price of approximately $14.80 - on $650M principal, with holders holding 'a one-time noncontingent right to require the Company to repurchase' on 'June 15, 2028'. The 2032 notes: 52.1832 shares per $1,000, approximately $19.16, on $1,150M. Red's numbers and red's date are verbatim correct. Blue's 41.5584 belongs to neither series. Blue introduced an error while purporting to fix one and demoted a correct verbatim finding to a guess. The conclusion is unaffected - both strikes are far out of the money at $11.52, so $1.8B of converts behave as straight debt either way, and the June-2028 put still collides with the Q4-2027 rent start - but the process failure is real and is the reason this escalates.

WHERE THAT LEAVES THE NAME. Both benches converge on no entry at $11.52 and I agree. Red's core survives even after the Texas correction: at any defensible cap rate, the fully-funded 175MW equity plus the actual net-debt drag does not clear a +50% bar without imputing well over a billion dollars to a mining business running roughly breakeven on ex-mark EBITDA and selling 98.8% of July production at $66,133. The Texas LOI is exclusivity, not a signed lease; it changes what the entry SIGNAL is, not what the asset is worth today.

THE MOST USEFUL THING I CAN SAY IS ABOUT THE GATE, NOT THE VERDICT. The ledger already carries a deck-provisional gate at alert_below 8.50. That gate is self-triggering and should not be armed as written. CLSK is ~1.0-beta to bitcoin; the Sandersville thesis is bitcoin-INDEPENDENT. A price gate at $8.50 will therefore be tripped by BTC falling roughly another quarter - at which point the mining leg is worth LESS and the treasury collateral backing the borrowing base has shrunk with it. The gate fires precisely when the thesis has gotten worse. A price gate is only valid when the price move is idiosyncratic to the thesis being gated. Here it is not. The gate must be either conditioned (price at or below $8.50 AND BTC not materially lower than today) or, better, replaced by the event gate: a DEFINITIVE lease on any tranche of the 885MW Texas portfolio, or the tenant named and rated. Red's doctrine line - 'debt-close news is not an entry signal' - is correct and survives; the tradeable event is the Texas conversion, not the financing.
blue_ruling: PARTIALLY OVERTURNED. Blue reduced red's single FATAL (the funded-prize ceiling) to SIZING on a scope-truncation argument, refuted red's venue-masking finding, and attempted to correct red's convertible-note conversion price. I re-verified all three legs against primary sources. Blue is RIGHT on two and WRONG on the third - and the third is the one blue presented as a correction of red.
reopen_gates: EVENT (primary, replaces the price gate as the lead trigger): a DEFINITIVE lease - not an LOI, not an extension of exclusivity - on any tranche of the 718-acre / up-to-885MW Texas portfolio. This re-rates the prize table multiplicatively and is the only event in the record that is both bitcoin-independent and company-controlled.

EVENT: the Sandersville tenant NAMED with a public rating. A genuine A-rated hyperscaler at a ~17% average-basis yield-on-cost re-rates the entire table; the adverse-selection prior is that exceptional economics from an unnamed 'high investment grade' counterparty is exactly the claim that most needs the name.

PRICE (demoted to secondary, and MUST BE CONDITIONED): price at or below ~$8.50-9.00 AND bitcoin not materially below today's ~$64-65k. Unconditioned, this gate is triggered BY the beta carrier at the moment the thesis is worst - see the verdict text. Do not arm the bare $8.50 alert.

DATA: closed project debt for Sandersville at a coupon at or below 8%, TOGETHER WITH disclosure that the $6.6B contracted base excludes expansion MW. Debt close ALONE is explicitly not an entry signal.

COVERAGE (open, and it is the decisive physical check): sentinel2_buildout on the Sandersville campus has never run - pre-flight failed to geocode 'Sandersville, Georgia' on both benches. The R1.13 facilities resolver now emits extra.lat/lon; resolve the Washington County GA parcel and run it. Capex pace against the Q4-CY2027 ready-for-service date is testable from orbit and nobody has looked.
